 FRESNO, Calif. (FOX26) — With less than two weeks until Election Day, Republican candidate for California governor Steve Hilton is pushing back against polling s howing him trailing Democrat Xavier Becerra. 
 Hilton sat down with FOX26's Madison Macay on Thursday to discuss his campaign, President Donald Trump's endorsement and immigration enforcement in the Central Valley.
 "I don't think anyone serious thinks that's what's really going on in California," Hilton said. "We'll see on election day. I think Emerson might have a lot of explaining to do."
 Hilton acknowledged the challenges facing his campaign, maintained he could still win.
 I think that while it's an uphill battle, I've always been clear about that, we can still win this election. When asked whether he would have done anything differently, Hilton pointed to fundraising.
 I wish we'd had more money. That's the honest truth. The conversation also turned to President Trump's endorsement during the primary and whether it may have cost Republicans the chance to have two candidates on the November ballot: 
 "Oh, no, that was never realistic," Hilton said. "That was always, I think, a fantasy."
 Hilton said he did not seek Trump's endorsement, but was honored to receive it. The conversation then turned to ICE detentions across the Central Valley, including cases FOX26 has reported involving people who say they had valid work permits. Hilton said his priority would be ensuring immigration enforcement focuses on dangerous criminals.
 "The first thing I would do on this issue is actually phone Tom Homan, who I know personally, say, right, what is going on?" Hilton said.
 He also said California's governor should be informed about federal immigration operations taking place in the state.
 "You can't be running operations in California without the governor knowing exactly what's happening and being part of the conversation," Hilton explained.
 When pressed about the impact on Central Valley agriculture and workers, Hilton said he would listen to local concerns.
 "So I'd be very concerned about that and ready to fight for this industry, including on that issue," he said.
 Hilton and Becerra face off in California's gubernatorial election on Nov. 3.
